examples.en: Sunlight comes into the balcony well.
I dried the laundry in the warm sun.

examples.ko: 고양이가 볕 좋은 창가에 누워 있어요.
examples.en: The cat is lying on the sunny window sill.
Winter sun is short but really warm.

examples.ko: 이 방은 볕이 안 들어서 조금 어두워요.
examples.en: This room gets no sun, so it is a little dark.
My face got tanned in the hot sun.

explain: '햇빛'은 해에서 오는 빛이고, '볕'은 그 빛이 주는 따뜻한 기운에 더 가까워요. 그래서 '볕이 들다', '볕을 쬐다'처럼 짝이 되는 동사와 함께 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '햇볕'이라는 형태로 더 많이 들려요.

phrases.en: The sunshine is warm, so I feel sleepy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '볕'보다 더 많이 들리는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form you hear more often than 볕 in daily talk.

phrases.en: The sun was nice today, so I went for a walk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 날씨가 맑고 햇살이 따뜻할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the day is clear and the sunlight is warm.

phrases.en: I dry the chili peppers in the sun.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빨래나 음식을 햇빛으로 말릴 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pair for drying laundry or food in the sun.

explain_en: 햇빛 is the light from the sun, while 볕 is closer to the warmth that light gives. It pairs with verbs such as 볕이 들다 and 볕을 쬐다. In daily speech you hear the form 햇볕 more often.

t90.ax: My face got tanned in the hot sun.

examples.ko: 올여름 불볕더위로 에어컨 없이는 못 살겠어요.
examples.en: With this summer's scorching heat, I cannot live without air conditioning.
The scorching heat has been going on for a week.

examples.ko: 불볕더위에는 낮에 밖에 오래 나가지 마세요.
examples.en: In scorching heat, do not stay outside for long during the day.

examples.ko: 이런 불볕더위 속에서 공사하시는 분들이 대단해요.
examples.en: The people who work on construction in this blazing heat are amazing.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 불볕더위 때문에 전기 사용량이 늘었다고 해요.
examples.en: The news says electricity use went up because of the scorching heat.
We went to a valley to escape the scorching heat.

explain: 햇볕이 쨍쨍 내리쬐는 심한 더위를 말해요. 습해서 후텁지근한 더위는 보통 '무더위'라고 해요. 뉴스에서는 '폭염'이라는 말도 같이 나와요.

phrases.en: Even in the scorching heat, the children run around outside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 심한 더위 속에서 무언가를 한다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone does something while in intense heat.

phrases.en: They say the scorching heat will continue this week too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더위가 며칠째 계속될 때 뉴스나 일상에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in news and daily talk when the heat lasts for days.

phrases.en: A heat wave warning was issued on the news today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '불볕더위'와 비슷한 뜻이고, 뉴스나 공식 안내에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Close in meaning to '불볕더위', but more common in news and official notices.

explain_en: It describes severe heat from a blazing sun. Humid, sticky heat is usually called '무더위'. In the news you will also see the word '폭염'.

examples.en: The kids picked up fallen pinecones in the park.
A squirrel is gnawing on a pinecone.
I made Christmas decorations myself from pinecones.
Lots of pinecones have fallen on the ground.
Pinecones open up when the weather is dry.
I received a single pinecone as a gift.

explain: 여기서 '솔'은 소나무를 뜻해서 솔방울은 소나무의 열매예요. 청소나 칫솔처럼 쓰는 '솔(brush)'과는 소리만 같은 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: Many pinecones have fallen on the forest path.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숲이나 공원에서 볼 수 있는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a scene you see in a forest or park.

phrases.en: I made a Christmas decoration out of pinecones.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재료로 쓴다는 뜻으로 '로'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '로' to show it is the material.

phrases.en: I brought home one pinecone as a souvenir.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수를 말할 때 '하나', '두 개'처럼 뒤에 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put a number like '하나' or '두 개' after it to count.

explain_en: Here '솔' means a pine tree, so 솔방울 is the cone of a pine. It is a different word from '솔' meaning a brush, as in toothbrush or cleaning brush; they only sound the same.

examples.en: The whole roof was blown away by the typhoon.
He lost every bit of the money he had.
I pulled the tree out entirely, roots and all.
That person took my heart completely.
The thief took the whole safe.

examples.ko: 그 일 때문에 생각이 송두리째 바뀌었어요.
examples.en: Because of that event, my way of thinking changed completely.

explain: '통째로'는 나누지 않고 전부라는 중립적인 말이고, 송두리째는 뿌리째 뽑히거나 다 잃는 것처럼 하나도 남지 않는 느낌이 강해요. 그래서 잃다, 빼앗기다, 뽑다 같은 말과 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: I pulled the weeds out by the roots.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뿌리까지 한꺼번에 뽑는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes pulling something out entirely, roots and all.

phrases.en: I was scammed and had all my money taken.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하나도 남기지 않고 다 빼앗길 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when everything is taken without anything left.

phrases.example: 몇 년 사이에 도시가 송두리째 바뀌었어요.
phrases.en: In a few years, the city changed completely.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일부가 아니라 전부가 달라졌을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when everything has changed, not just a part.

explain_en: The whole thing, all at once, often loss (송두리째) '통째로' is neutral and means as a whole without dividing, while 송두리째 strongly suggests nothing is left, as when something is pulled out by the roots or lost entirely. It pairs well with verbs like 잃다, 빼앗기다 and 뽑다.

t90.ax: The thief took the whole safe.

en: to sweep; to wipe out; to sweep away

examples.en: I swept all the leaves in the yard away with a broom.
A huge flood swept away the small village.
I feel refreshed after sweeping away the dust.
The kids polished off the snacks in no time.
Let's sweep away all our worries and start fresh.
I sweep up the hair on the floor in one go.

explain: '쓸다'에 '-어 버리다'가 붙어 깨끗이 없애 버린다는 느낌이 강해요. 먼지뿐 아니라 홍수나 태풍이 휩쓸어 가는 것, 음식을 다 먹어 치우는 것에도 비유로 써요. 사람에게 쓰면 거친 말이 되니 조심하세요.

phrases.example: 눈이 오기 전에 낙엽을 다 쓸어버리자.
phrases.en: Let's sweep away all the leaves before the snow comes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구나 가족에게 편하게 권하는 반말 청유형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual suggestion form used with friends or family.

phrases.en: After sweeping the snow away, I moved the car out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깨끗이 치운 뒤에 다음 일을 말할 때 이어서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to link to the next action after clearing something away.

phrases.en: I was so hungry that I wolfed down all the rice.
phrases.nuance_ko: '싹'이 붙으면 하나도 남기지 않고 먹거나 치운다는 느낌이 강해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '싹' stresses that nothing is left, whether eaten or cleared.

explain_en: Sweep everything away in one go — forceful, casual to dramatic. It adds '-어 버리다' to '쓸다', giving a strong feeling of clearing something away completely. Beyond dust, it is used for floods or storms sweeping things off and, figuratively, for eating up food. Used about people, it becomes a rough expression.

t90.ax: A huge flood swept away the small village.

examples.en: There is a low hill behind my house.
Every weekend I climb the hill and exercise.
I picked up chestnuts on the hill with my grandmother.
This village is surrounded by low hills.

examples.ko: 야산 아래에 작은 절이 하나 있어요.
examples.en: There is a small temple at the foot of the hill.
I heard the wildfire is spreading toward the hill.

explain: 높고 큰 산은 그냥 '산'이라고 하고, 마을 가까이에 있는 낮은 산은 '야산'이라고 해요. 산책하러 가는 동네 산을 떠올리면 돼요. '뒷산'은 집 뒤에 있다는 위치를 강조해서 불러요.

phrases.en: I climb the hill every Sunday morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높지 않은 산이라서 가볍게 다녀오는 느낌으로 '오르다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Because the hill is low, '오르다' gives the feeling of a light, easy climb.

phrases.en: I take a walk on the hill behind my house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 야산 중에서도 집 뒤에 있다는 위치를 강조할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this for a low hill when you want to stress that it is behind your home.

phrases.en: I picked up acorns on the hill in our neighborhood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마을 가까이에 있는 낮은 산이라는 뜻을 더 분명하게 보여 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: This makes it clearer that the hill is low and close to the village.

explain_en: Low unmanaged hill near town — everyday weekend walks. A tall, big mountain is just 산, while a low mountain near a village is 야산. Picture the neighborhood hill you go to for a walk. 뒷산 stresses that the hill is located behind the house.

examples.en: We found an oasis in the desert.

examples.ko: 바쁜 도시에서 이 카페는 제게 오아시스예요.
examples.en: In this busy city, this cafe is an oasis for me.
Palm trees grow around the oasis.

examples.ko: 오늘 먹은 시원한 수박이 오아시스 같았어요.
examples.en: The cold watermelon I ate today felt like an oasis.

examples.ko: 그 도서관은 학생들에게 오아시스 같은 곳이에요.
examples.en: That library is like an oasis for students.
The camels drank water at the oasis.

explain: 사막에서 물이 있는 곳이지만, 한국어에서는 '바쁘고 힘든 곳 속의 쉼터'라는 비유로도 많이 써요. '도심 속 오아시스'처럼 광고나 기사에서 자주 나와요. '쉼터'는 앉아서 쉬는 실제 장소에 가깝고, 오아시스는 지친 마음을 살려 주는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: an oasis in the middle of the city
phrases.nuance_ko: 복잡한 도시 한가운데에서 조용히 쉴 수 있는 곳을 소개할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to introduce a quiet place to rest in the middle of a crowded city.

explain_en: It is the watered spot in a desert, but Korean also uses it widely as a metaphor for a refuge in a busy, tough place. It often appears in ads and articles as '도심 속 오아시스'. '쉼터' is closer to a real place to sit and rest, while 오아시스 carries a feeling of reviving a tired mind.

examples.ko: 어제 마당에 운석이 떨어졌다는 뉴스를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a news story that a meteorite fell in a yard yesterday.
I touched a real meteorite at the museum.

examples.ko: 운석 조각을 비싼 값에 사는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people buy meteorite pieces at high prices.
I gave a presentation about meteorites in science class.
I saw people looking for meteorites in the desert.

examples.ko: 떨어진 운석 때문에 지붕에 구멍이 났어요.
examples.en: The fallen meteorite made a hole in the roof.

explain: 하늘에서 불타며 떨어지는 빛은 '별똥별'(유성), 땅에 떨어져 남은 돌이 운석이에요. 일상에서는 '별똥별'을 더 자주 말하고, 운석은 뉴스나 과학 이야기에 나와요.

phrases.en: A meteorite fell in the forest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운석이 땅에 닿았을 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the most common phrase for a meteorite landing.

phrases.example: 큰 운석 충돌 때문에 공룡이 사라졌다고 해요.
phrases.en: They say dinosaurs disappeared because of a big meteorite impact.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과학 이야기에서 자주 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This often appears in science talk.

phrases.en: They found a meteorite in Antarctica.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땅에서 운석을 찾았을 때 '발견하다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it with 발견하다 when a meteorite is found on the ground.

explain_en: The streak of light burning in the sky is a 별똥별 (shooting star), and the rock that lands on the ground is a 운석. In daily talk people say 별똥별 more often; 운석 appears in news and science topics.

examples.en: I hear a lunar eclipse will happen tonight.

examples.ko: 월식 때는 달이 붉게 보일 때가 있어요.
examples.en: During a lunar eclipse, the moon sometimes looks red.
I watched the lunar eclipse with my family.

examples.ko: 월식은 지구 그림자가 달을 가릴 때 생겨요.
examples.en: A lunar eclipse happens when Earth's shadow covers the moon.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 다음 월식 시간을 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: The news announced the time of the next lunar eclipse.

examples.ko: 월식과 일식의 차이를 과학 시간에 배웠어요.
examples.en: I learned the difference between lunar and solar eclipses in science class.

explain: 해가 가려지는 건 '일식'이에요. 달이 완전히 가려질 때는 '개기월식'이라고 해요. 뉴스에서는 '월식이 일어나다', '월식을 관측하다'처럼 말해요.

phrases.en: There was a total lunar eclipse last night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 달이 완전히 가려지는 월식이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A lunar eclipse where the moon is fully covered.

phrases.en: We observed the lunar eclipse with a telescope.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과학 수업이나 뉴스에서 자주 쓰는 딱딱한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal phrase often used in science class and news.

phrases.en: I watched the lunar eclipse from the rooftop.
phrases.nuance_ko: '관측하다'보다 일상적으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: More casual than 관측하다.

explain_en: When the sun is covered it is 일식 (solar eclipse). A total lunar eclipse is 개기월식. News uses 월식이 일어나다 and 월식을 관측하다.

examples.ko: 이 지역에서는 겨울에도 키울 수 있는 작물을 많이 심어요.
examples.en: In this area, they plant a lot of crops that can be grown even in winter.

examples.ko: 올해는 비가 적어서 작물이 잘 자라지 않았어요.
examples.en: There was little rain this year, so the crops didn't grow well.

examples.ko: 아버지는 새로운 작물을 시험해 보려고 밭을 넓히셨어요.
examples.en: My father expanded the field to try out a new crop.

examples.ko: 태풍이 지나간 뒤에 작물 피해를 조사했어요.
examples.en: After the typhoon passed, they surveyed the crop damage.

examples.ko: 쌀 말고 다른 작물도 키워 보고 싶어요?
examples.en: Do you want to try growing crops other than rice?

examples.ko: 이 땅은 어떤 작물이든 잘 자라는 좋은 땅이에요.
examples.en: This is good land where any crop grows well.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '채소', '곡식'처럼 구체적으로 말하고, 작물은 농사 이야기나 뉴스에서 더 자주 나와요. 한 지역에서 키우는 식물을 통틀어 말할 때 편해요. '농작물'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: The typhoon caused great damage to crops.
phrases.nuance_ko: '작물'과 거의 같은 말인데 농사로 키운 것임을 더 분명히 보여 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same as 작물 but makes clear it's farm-grown produce.

phrases.example: 이 마을에서는 여러 가지 작물을 재배해요.
phrases.en: This village grows many kinds of crops.
phrases.nuance_ko: '재배하다'와 함께 쓰면 농사 이야기에 잘 맞아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paired with 재배하다, it fits well in talk about farming.

phrases.en: I planted crops in the field in spring.
phrases.nuance_ko: 씨앗이나 모종을 땅에 심는 때에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when planting seeds or seedlings in the ground.

explain_en: In daily talk people say 'chaeso' (vegetables) or 'gokshik' (grains) specifically; 작물 shows up more in farming talk and the news. It is handy for the plants grown in an area as a whole. You can also say 농작물.

examples.en: It rained, so the playground is muddy.
The ground was soggy and my shoes got soaked.

examples.ko: 비 온 뒤에는 길이 질어서 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: After rain the road is muddy, so be careful.
Rice that is too soft and wet doesn't taste good.

examples.ko: 반죽이 질게 되면 밀가루를 더 넣으세요.
examples.en: If the dough gets too wet, add more flour.

examples.ko: 오늘은 길이 질지 않아서 걷기 좋아요.
examples.en: The road isn't muddy today, so it's good for walking.

explain: '질다'는 땅이나 밥, 반죽에 물기가 너무 많을 때 써요. 반대는 '되다'(밥이 되다)예요. 'ㄹ' 받침 때문에 '진 길', '지니까'처럼 ㄹ이 빠져요. 사람에게 쓰는 말이 아니에요.

phrases.example: 비 온 뒤라 진 길을 조심해서 걸었어요.
phrases.en: After the rain, I walked carefully on the muddy road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 'ㄹ'이 빠져서 '질다'가 '진'으로 바뀌어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The ㄹ drops, so 질다 becomes 진.

phrases.en: I added too much water, so the rice is mushy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 밥에 물기가 너무 많을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when rice has too much moisture.

phrases.example: 오늘은 땅이 질지 않아서 걷기 편해요.
phrases.en: The ground isn't muddy today, so it's easy to walk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물기가 적당할 때 부정형으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used when the moisture is just right.

explain_en: '질다' describes ground, rice or dough that has too much moisture. The opposite is '되다' (as in rice being firm). Because the stem ends in ㄹ, the ㄹ drops: '진 길', '지니까'. It isn't used for people.

examples.en: A storm battered us all night.
The flight was cancelled because of the storm.
The ship ran into a storm and returned to port.
After the storm passed, the sky cleared.
It was a storm strong enough to shake the windows.
My umbrella flipped inside out in the storm.

explain: 세찬 바람과 비가 함께 오는 날씨예요. '태풍'은 여름과 가을에 오는 이름 붙은 큰 폭풍이고, '폭풍우'는 규모와 상관없이 비바람이 거센 상태를 가리켜요. 소설이나 뉴스에서 '폭풍우가 몰아치다'로 많이 써요.

phrases.en: After the storm passed, the sky cleared up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비바람이 끝났을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the storm is over.

phrases.en: The wind and rain were so strong that my umbrella broke.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '폭풍우'보다 더 쉽고 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier word than 폭풍우 that is common in everyday speech.

phrases.en: A typhoon will come this weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 태풍은 이름이 붙는 큰 폭풍이고, 폭풍우는 규모와 상관없어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typhoon is a big named storm, while 폭풍우 can be of any size.

explain_en: 폭풍우 is weather with strong wind and rain together. 태풍 is the named big storm of summer and autumn, while 폭풍우 describes any fierce wind-and-rain regardless of scale. You often see 폭풍우가 몰아치다 in novels and news.

en: to take refuge; to be evacuated; to flee

examples.en: Residents flee up the mountain.

examples.ko: 지진 때 우리 가족은 학교로 피난했어요.
examples.en: During the earthquake, my family took shelter at the school.

examples.ko: 태풍이 오면 높은 곳으로 피난할 거예요.
examples.en: If a typhoon comes, we will evacuate to higher ground.
The road was full of people fleeing.
A fire broke out, so we evacuated quickly and called.

examples.ko: 집이 물에 잠겨서 친척 집으로 피난해야 했어요.
examples.en: My house was flooded, so I had to take refuge at a relative's.

explain: 재난이나 전쟁에서 안전한 곳으로 가는 거예요. '대피하다'가 뉴스에서 더 자주 나오고, '피난하다'는 오래 떠나 있는 이야기에 어울려요. 몸만 피하는 '피하다'와는 달라서 장소로 옮겨 갈 때 써요.

phrases.example: 홍수 때문에 높은 곳으로 피난을 갔어요.
phrases.en: Because of the flood, we fled to higher ground.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '피난'과 함께 쓰는 가장 흔한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common expression using the noun 피난.

phrases.en: A fire broke out, so everyone evacuated outside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 당장 몸을 피하는 느낌이고 뉴스에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels like getting out of danger right now; common in the news.

phrases.en: The people who evacuated are staying in the gym.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사가 뒤의 명사를 꾸며 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the verb describes the noun that follows.

explain_en: Move away from a typhoon, war or disaster; often organized (높은 지대로 피난하다) It means going to a safe place in a disaster or war. 대피하다 shows up more in the news, while 피난하다 suits stories of being away for longer. Unlike plain 피하다 (avoid), it implies moving to another location.

examples.en: I felt sympathy after hearing that story.
I helped him out of sympathy.

examples.ko: 아이들은 길 잃은 강아지에게 동정심을 느꼈어요.
examples.en: The children felt pity for the lost puppy.

examples.ko: 뉴스를 보면 동정심 많은 사람들이 기부를 해요.
examples.en: On the news, compassionate people make donations.
Sympathy alone can't solve the problem.

examples.ko: 나는 그 사람에게 동정심이 하나도 안 들어요.
examples.en: I don't feel any sympathy for that person.

explain: '동정심이 생기다/들다', '동정심을 느끼다'처럼 써요. 불쌍하게 여기는 마음이라서 상대가 자기를 낮춰 본다고 느낄 수 있어서 '동정하지 마세요'라고 싫어하는 사람도 있어요. 더 깊고 따뜻한 마음은 '연민'이라고 하고, 글에서 많이 써요.

phrases.en: I felt sympathy when I saw the stray cat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불쌍한 대상을 보고 마음이 움직일 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for being moved by seeing someone in a pitiful situation.

phrases.en: My younger sibling is very compassionate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남의 어려움을 잘 불쌍히 여기는 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a person who easily feels for others in trouble.

phrases.en: I feel sorry for that person's situation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동정심을 동사로 말한 것이고, 상대를 낮게 본다는 느낌이 들 수도 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form; it can sometimes sound like looking down on someone.

explain_en: Neutral — kind feeling toward someone suffering (동정심이 생기다) You say '동정심이 생기다/들다' or '동정심을 느끼다'. Because it means feeling sorry for someone, the other person may feel looked down on, and some people say '동정하지 마세요' (don't pity me). '연민' is a deeper, warmer feeling and is used more in writing.

t90.ax: I helped him out of sympathy.
